newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Moroccan PM holds cooperation talks in Libya.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan PM holds cooperation talks in Libya.

text.p: Moroccan Prime Minister Abdellatif Filali is in Tripoli for talks with Libyan officials on boosting bilateral economic cooperation, the official Libyan news agency JANA reported on Wednesday.

JANA, monitored in Tunis, said Filali on Tuesday night co-chaired with his Libyan counterpart Abdelmajid al-Gu'ud the opening session of the joint cooperation committee. The session was also attended by businessmen from the two countries.

"Businessmen from Tunisia and from Egypt have already visited Libya to discuss joint ventures, and I take this opportunity to call for a meeting between businessmen and investors from Morocco, Tunisia, Libya and Egypt with the aim of contributing to unity between the four Arab countries," JANA quoted Gu'ud as saying at the session.
"We call for more efforts to reach the establishment of a free trade zone and a full partnership between Libya and Morocco," he added.

Gu'ud said among areas of possible cooperation between Libya and Morocco were drugs manufacturing, textiles and clothes, leather, car's manufacturing and marketing, banking and financial investments, agriculture and water resources.

"Joint economic projects would contribute to boost the excellent relations between Libya and Morocco and respond to the ambitions of the Libyan revolution leader (Muammar Gaddafi) and King Hassan of Morocco," JANA quoted Filali as saying.
Libya and Morocco are members along with Tunisia, Algeria and Mauritania of the Arab Maghreb Union established in 1989 with the aim of establishing an economic grouping.
